annotations.title: Check if the Internet Is Down

description: Is there a shared-infrastructure incident right now (Cloudflare, an AWS region, a CDN), as inferred from RealUptime's own checks across every service it tracks? Answers one of three levels: "ok" (no shared incident; a count of services whose checks fail travels with the catalog size), "provider_incident" (our checks fail for at least five services sharing one provider signal while our checks of services on other providers mostly pass; the provider is named with the services affected and a confidence sentence), or "several_unrelated" (our checks fail for several services with no shared provider signal). Also returns the dependency map from our checks: how many tracked services answer from behind each provider. A provider incident is a CORRELATION of our check readings, never a cause the provider stated, and it changes no service's own verdict; ask is_service_down for a specific service. Takes no arguments. Readings are RealUptime's own check readings, never user reports. For a service whose status feed we can read, `vendor.feed_working` is true and `vendor` holds the vendor's own declared incident from its status page: that statement leads and gives the verdict and plate, and `checks_reading` and `vendor.regional_reading` are our check reading beside it, never a second outage. Where we cannot read a feed (`vendor.feed_working` false), the answer is our checks alone. "blocked" means our check was refused, which is NOT a failed check of the service. A no-data answer is never a passing check. Our check readings are our own reading from outside, not the service's official status. `check_evidence`, when it is not null, says what a pass of this service's check shows and does not show: repeat it with any claim that the service works. Cite the returned source.url when repeating any of this.
name: is_the_internet_down
